draft.summary: Nepal's food delivery market is centered primarily in Kathmandu and expanding to cities like Pokhara and Chitwan. Foodmandu, founded in 2010, is the market leader with over 1,000 partner restaurants and processes thousands of orders daily. Other players include Pathao Food, Bhoj, and BhojMandu, though the market remains nascent with limited publicly available revenue and sizing data specific to Nepal. The COVID-19 lockdown period accelerated adoption of food and grocery delivery services in the Kathmandu Valley.

It has expanded into groceries and essentials through Foodmandu Fresh and One Mart, and has raised Series B funding from investors including Team Ventures and True North Associates.

observations: Foodmandu is Nepal's leading food delivery service, operating since 2010 with over 1,000 partner restaurants across Kathmandu, Pokhara, and Chitwan, processing thousands of orders daily and expanding into grocery delivery through Foodmandu Fresh and One Mart. [F2, F5, F9]

The Kathmandu-based food delivery startup ecosystem includes multiple players: Bhoj (founded 2014), BhojMandu (2020), and Foodganj (2020), though most remain unfunded apart from Foodmandu, which has raised Series B funding from investors including Team Ventures and True North Associates. [F8]

Nepal's online grocery segment appears to have a notable number of startups — one tracking source's title references 33 online grocery startups in the country — with investors including British International Investment (London) and local firms like Rosebay Consulting active in Kathmandu. [F6]

Food delivery companies in the Kathmandu Valley played an essential role during the COVID-19 lockdown by delivering groceries and vegetables door-to-door, though they faced significant operational challenges during this period. [F4]

Globally, the food delivery market was valued at approximately $118 billion in 2021 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of about 12.8% through 2033, providing a broader growth context for Nepal's emerging market. [F10]

Pathao Food is mentioned alongside Foodmandu in a document about Nepal's food delivery market, suggesting it is a recognized participant in the sector, though substantive details on its operations are not available in the findings. [F7]

issues: The brief includes two observations that rely on BACKGROUND findings: observation 5 uses F10 (a global market figure marked as BACKGROUND), and this is the only BACKGROUND-based observation allowed, which is fine. However, the observation quotes specific dollar figures ($118 billion) from a global report (F10) that is not Nepal-specific, which is acceptable as general context but should be clearly framed as such — it already is, so this is borderline acceptable.

The Pathao Food observation (observation 6) is very thin. F7 is essentially just a Scribd document title with no substantive content — the finding contains no actual data, analysis, or details beyond the document title. Citing F7 to claim Pathao Food is a 'significant competitor' shaping Nepal's food delivery landscape overstates what the finding supports. The finding only shows the existence of a document discussing Foodmandu and Pathao Food together.

The competitors section lists Foodmandu as a competitor, but for a market request the competitors should be key players competing within the market, not the market leader described as a competitor to itself. Having both Foodmandu and Pathao Food is reasonable for a market request, but Foodmandu's note reads more like a company profile than a competitor note. This is a minor structural concern.

Observation 3 about '33 online grocery startups' cites F6, but F6's content is heavily fragmented and mostly shows investor names and startup names without clear confirmation of the '33 startups' count beyond the source title. The number appears in the source title, so this is marginally supported but the observation should be more cautious.
